chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Learning organ from Wild Bill Davis at Wells
summary: After hours at Little Belmont he heard Wild Bill Davis, learned organ on Wells's instrument, and found it hard to leave percussive piano sound.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, after hours you would go to the Club Harlem, and you heard Wild Bill Davis at Little Belmont.
The Little Belmont was across from Club Harlem.

Well, when I heard him, he was great. I loved the way he played it. I said, 'Well, that's for me.' He used to make that organ sing. And that's how I started playing organ. When he came up to John(?) Wells' place, he had an organ and piano. Well, the piano players would sit in! So Mr. Wells, eventually he said, 'You know, you and Marlowe Morris and the rest of the gang, and Bill Doggett, owe me an organ, because you learned on my organ!'
You were a very experienced piano player by this time. But was it hard to switch over to organ?

Well, yes, in a way. If you played piano... If you didn't play a good piano, it would be a cinch for you to play that hot Jazz organ. But I mean, when you... At that time, when you were a piano player, that's...you know... It was such a tremendous... The thing is to divorce yourself from the percussive sound to another sound. And I liked the way...
